articles.title: SEC filing: 8-K — Fermi Inc. (CURRENT REPORT)
articles.summary: Fermi Inc. has issued $431.25 million in aggregate principal amount of 5.00% convertible senior notes due 2031, with total net proceeds of approximately $416.81 million, which will be used for general corporate purposes. The notes are convertible into cash, shares of common stock, or a combination thereof, and have a conversion rate initially set at 105.0862 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes. The company also entered into capped call transactions to reduce potential dilution to its common stock upon conversion of the notes, using approximately $34.5 million of the net proceeds to pay for these transactions.

articles.title: SEC filing: 8-K — Fermi Inc. (CURRENT REPORT)
articles.summary: Fermi Inc. discloses the immediate resignation of director Miles Everson, effective July 10, 2026, due to a disagreement over access to company books and records and the delegation of responsibility for overseeing financing transactions to the Finance Committee. Everson, a designee of Toby Neugebauer, did not serve on any committee of the Board at the time of his resignation. The company believes Everson was granted full access to its books and records, except for materials related to pending litigation involving Neugebauer.

articles.title: SEC filing: 8-K — Fermi Inc. (CURRENT REPORT)
articles.summary: Fermi Inc. commenced an offering of $350 million in convertible senior notes due 2031 to qualified institutional buyers, with an option for the initial purchasers to buy an additional $52.5 million in notes. The company plans to use the net proceeds to pay for capped call transactions and for general corporate purposes. Fermi Inc. also disclosed that it has deferred its planned election to be taxed as a real estate investment trust, and now expects to make this election for its taxable year ending December 31, 2026, if it qualifies.

Neugebauer, Vicksburg Investments Management LLC, and other parties have withdrawn their solicitation to call a special meeting of Fermi Inc. shareholders due to an untenable timeline caused by a judge's recusal in pending litigation. The special meeting was intended to address entrenching actions taken by the company's directors, but the parties will not act on any agent designations received from shareholders unless the solicitation is resumed. The withdrawal is a result of the recent development in the Texas Business Court litigation between the parties and the company.

articles.title: SEC filing: DFAN14A — Fermi Inc. (DEFINITIVE ADDITIONAL MATERIALS)
articles.summary: Toby R. Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., has suspended his proxy campaign to call a special meeting of shareholders due to a judge's last-minute recusal, which has disrupted the timeline for the strategic process. Despite having earned the backing of over 70% of votes cast and proxy advisory firms Glass Lewis and Egan-Jones, Neugebauer will continue to push for good governance through the judicial process. Neugebauer remains confident in Fermi's ability to secure a tenant group and achieve long-term success, particularly with its valuable asset Project Matador.

articles.title: SEC filing: DFAN14A — Fermi Inc. (DEFINITIVE ADDITIONAL MATERIALS)
articles.summary: Toby R. Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., disclosed that the company has dropped its lawsuit against him, which was filed in response to his challenge of the validity of the company's 70% supermajority bylaw. This move comes after the Texas Business Court ordered Fermi to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw, and Neugebauer claims that the company's decision to abandon the lawsuit confirms that the bylaw was adopted to entrench the board's power. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players.

articles.title: SEC filing: DFAN14A — Fermi Inc. (DEFINITIVE ADDITIONAL MATERIALS)
articles.summary: Toby R. Neugebauer, co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi America, delivered an investor presentation on June 30, 2026, discussing his concerns about the company's contracts and governance. Neugebauer emphasized the importance of having the right team to steward contracts, which can be either assets or liabilities, and expressed his desire for an independent committee and a banker-led market test to ensure evidence-based decision-making. He also stated that he is not interested in returning to the company, but rather wants to ensure that the board prioritizes the interests of shareholders.
